title: Capacity constraints & reserve scenario planning - Nimbus Health
next_steps: Maya to send reserved capacity pricing worksheet and example cost delta
Carlos to share private deployment checklist and sample VPC diagram
Customer to provide 2-week sample traffic traces and cold-start profile
action_items: Maya (Redwood) | Send reserved vs on-demand pricing CSV and a two-year cost model | 2026-12-07
Carlos (Redwood) | Share Private deployment checklist + sample VPC diagram (link) | 2026-12-04
Dave (Nimbus) | Provide 14-day request logs and percentiles for p50/p95/p99 | 2026-12-03
summary: Discovery call focused on sizing reserved GPU pools, tenant isolation needs for PHI workloads, burst strategy (hot pool vs pre-warm), and acceptable tradeoffs for latency vs unit cost. Redwood AE+SE clarified options: Hosted API for quick start, Dedicated reserved pools for isolation and predictability, Private/VPC for compliance. Action items include pricing worksheet, private-deploy checklist, and sample traffic for benching.
transcript:
[00:00] AE - Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — going to do a quick intro, I'm Maya, account lead for Redwood. Carlos is our solutions engineer. Could folks intro quickly?
[00:12] CTO - Priya (Nimbus): Hi Maya, Priya here, CTO at Nimbus Health. We run several clinical workflows that hit LLM endpoints for triage and note summarization — main concern is PHI isolation and predictable costs.
[00:22] Infra - Dave (Nimbus): Dave here, infra lead. We manage our Kubernetes clusters and a mix of GCP and on-prem GPUs. We want reserved capacity that won't cause noisy-neighbor problems.
[00:30] SE - Carlos (Redwood): Great, thanks. Quick outline: sizing and reserve questions, isolation options (dedicated vs private), burst patterns and hot pooling, and then next steps for a pilot.
[00:48] PM - Anika (Nimbus): Timeline wise, we want a pilot in Q1 and production by Q2 if things look good.
[00:55] AE - Maya: Perfect. Dave, can you share a bit about your current traffic shape — are you spiky with periodic day peaks or more steady?
[01:05] Infra - Dave: It's spiky. We have nightly batch summarization and daytime interactive triage. The interactive peaks are short but high qps for like 3-10 minutes. Cold-starts are painful; startup latency on some models is 1.2s plus. We looked at pre-warming but not sure cost tradeoffs.
[01:28] SE - Carlos: Makes sense. For Dedicated Reserved pools we typically recommend a hot pool + overflow routing. Hot pool keeps a set of prewarmed replicas with KV cache warmed so tail latency stays low; overflow can hit lower-cost variants or hosted endpoints. Do you have an internal threshold for p99 latency?
[01:48] CTO - Priya: We need p99 < 350ms for the triage call path. For batch jobs p95 can be looser.
[01:56] SE - Carlos: Ok that's helpful. Two levers: increase hot pool size to reduce queuing and prewarm to reduce model cold starts. Prewarming is a steady cost; hot pool sizing is about concurrency and token-rate.
[02:12] Infra - Dave: Quick question — how isolated is Dedicated? We have to prove PHI is never on shared hardware for audits.
[02:20] AE - Maya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and tenant isolation at the node level; we can combine that with Private deployment in your VPC if you need customer-managed networking and exhaustive audit logs. For SOC2 evidence we provide audit logs, SSO/SAML integration, and KMS key wrapping options.
[02:38] PM - Anika: Do you have examples of customers with mixed on-prem + cloud footprints?
[02:44] SE - Carlos: Yes, we've done hybrid where control plane is Redwood hosted but inference plane is customer private — we supply the deployment artifacts. There can be network egress constraints to work through.
[02:54] [03:01] CTO - Priya: On burst, if we reserve 8 GPUs does Redwood allow bursting beyond commitment? We don't want to throttle if we have a sudden event.
[03:12] AE - Maya: Yes, we support burst into shared capacity subject to availability; customers on reserved contracts get prioritized routing and can configure burst policies. There is a cost delta for burst usage — typically billed at higher on-demand rates.
[03:26] Infra - Dave: Are GPUs pinned to the customer in Dedicated? Like physical tenancy?
[03:31] SE - Carlos: For Dedicated reserved pools we allocate whole nodes to you — logical isolation with cgroups and vGPU allocation; for physical single-tenant nodes we can discuss dedicated tenancy options (additional fee). If you need absolute physical tenancy we can include that in an enterprise contract.
[03:51] PM - Anika: How do you handle model variants? We plan to run several model sizes for different latencies.
[03:58] SE - Carlos: You can pin model variants to different node pools. Smaller models on cheaper instances and larger ones on high-memory GPUs. Smart routing can send requests to fallback model if primary is unavailable. That helps reduce cost while preserving availability.
[04:16] [04:30] CTO - Priya: Security specific: we need to ensure keys are customer-managed. Does Redwood integrate with our KMS?
[04:38] AE - Maya: Yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed key material in Private deployments. For hosted we provide envelope encryption options and SOC2 artifacts; for Private you control the KMS.
[04:48] Infra - Dave: For cost modeling — how do we estimate token cost vs reservation cost? We have ~500k tokens/day average but with 10x spikes.
[04:59] SE - Carlos: We'll run a cost model: split steady-state into reserved capacity and estimate hot pool cost + prewarm minutes; spikes going to burst. We usually ask for two weeks of traffic to simulate. Could you send hashes (or anonymized) of request sizes and qps by minute?
[05:15] Infra - Dave: Yes we can provide anonymized traces.
[05:19] AE - Maya: Great. One thing to note — KV cache hit rates matter a lot. If your workload reuses prefixes a lot, effective cost drops because tokens served from KV cache are cheaper.
[05:30] PM - Anika: What about observability — can we get token-level billing and per-route latency?
[05:36] SE - Carlos: Redwood Console exposes per-route token breakdown, latency percentiles, error rates, and tracing hooks. You can also export logs to your SIEM.
[05:45] [06:00] CTO - Priya: For the pilot, what would be success criteria?
[06:05] AE - Maya: I'd propose pilot success = meet p99 target for interactive path under your production-ish load, cost within X% of model, and smooth rollout automation tested. We can define exact numbers in SLO doc.
[06:18] PM - Anika: Timeline: if pricing looks good, we can sign pilot by mid-December and start Jan 6th.
[06:26] AE - Maya: Sounds feasible. We'll get you a pilot plan and pricing.
[06:30] [06:45] Infra - Dave: A technical detail — do you do kernel selection and quantized runtimes in Dedicated? We rely on int8 for smaller GPUs.
[06:54] SE - Carlos: Yes, runtime picks optimized kernels (we call it kernel selection) based on model and sequence length; quantized paths are supported on dedicated infra. We also have sequence-length aware batching to reduce latency for interactive sessions.
[07:08] CTO - Priya: What about failover — if a node goes down in our reserved pool, what's the recovery?
[07:16] SE - Carlos: Autoscaling and cross-zone redundancy helps. We recommend Reserve + 10% buffer for node failures. There's also automatic fallback to hosted if private capacity is exhausted. We'll show our playbook.
[07:30] PM - Anika: Any compliance artifacts we should see early?
[07:34] AE - Maya: We'll attach SOC2 report, data processing agreement, and private deployment checklist. Carlos will send the VPC diagram.
[07:42] [08:00] Infra - Dave: Small nit — are there any hard limits on concurrent KV cache size per tenant? We have large context windows.
[08:09] SE - Carlos: Limits are configurable; for very large KV/cache we may recommend larger GPU memory instances or sharded cache. We'll include guidance.
[08:20] CTO - Priya: Pricing question — if we commit 16 GPUs for 12 months, how much discount vs on-demand?
[08:29] AE - Maya: Typical discount bands are in the 25-45% range depending on term and commitment. We'll model conservative 30% and show scenario table.
[08:38] [09:00] PM - Anika: A typical objection from finance: what happens if usage decreases after commit?
[09:06] AE - Maya: We have options: flexible commit tiers, conversion credits, or step-down windows in enterprise deals. We'll outline options.
[09:16] CTO - Priya: For the pilot we want to run a benchmark: 1) baseline latency on our model, 2) hot-pool sized run, 3) burst to hosted. Can Redwood run 99th percentile synthetic tests?
[09:29] SE - Carlos: Yes we can run bench harness against the reserved pool using your traces; we also support spike replay to measure tail. We'll need the anonymized traces and model artifacts (or model spec).
[09:43] Infra - Dave: Do you support GPU family mixing in the same pool? We might want A10s for smaller models and H100s for large.
[09:52] SE - Carlos: You can have separate node pools and route by model. Mixed pools complicate scheduling; we usually keep homogeneous pools per model class.
[10:05] [10:30] AE - Maya: Ok I'll summarize next steps: send pricing worksheet, share private deploy checklist, collect 14 days of traces, schedule bench run. Anything else?
[10:40] PM - Anika: Please include a simple cost-per-req example and a chart showing break-even points for hot pool vs burst.
[10:47] AE - Maya: Will do.
[10:50] CTO - Priya: One more — we have a procurement window in late Jan; if pilot goes well we need 60 days lead time for GPU procurement for on-prem hardware.
[11:00] AE - Maya: Noted. We'll aim timelines accordingly.
[11:05] SE - Carlos: I'll attach some case studies with similar regulated customers.
[11:12] [11:30] AE - Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the attachments and proposed dates.
[11:36] CTO - Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[11:40] Infra - Dave: Thanks.
[11:42] PM - Anika: Thanks all.
notes: Customer emphasized PHI isolation and evidence for audits
Pilot success criteria: p99 < 350ms for triage path, cost within target range, automation tested
Action items focus on pricing, traces, and private deployment artifacts
